name: Corset brace

card.summary: A corset-style lumbar support with elastic fabric and boning, worn to hold the torso upright and steady the lower back.
card.note: Long-term reliance has been linked in the corset literature to weaker core muscles; medical braces are prescribed for specific conditions.

quick.overview:
A corset brace is a lumbar support that resembles a historical corset, usually elastic fabric with plastic or metal boning. It holds the lower back and torso in place, so people wear it for an upright, steadier posture while it is on.

It is used medically for lower-back pain and after spinal surgery, and in a small study of adolescents with spondylolysis a corset brace changed spine movement during daily activity. Lifters also use similar belts for support under load.
quick.how: The brace wraps around the lower torso and fastens with hooks, laces or straps, worn over or under clothing for set periods, sometimes under clinician direction.
quick.risks: Reviews of historical corset use link long-term wear to weakened core and back muscles, reliance on the garment for upright posture, and reduced lung capacity with tight lacing. Medical braces are normally prescribed for a condition.

lead: A corset brace is a medical-style lumbar support that resembles a corset. Modern versions use elastic fabric with flexible plastic boning, with metal boning where more rigidity is needed, and they are used to prevent and treat lower-back pain and sometimes after spinal surgery.[1]

For appearance, the draw is that the garment holds the torso upright while worn, giving a straighter posture and a smoother torso line under clothing. A 2021 study of five adolescents with spondylolysis measured spine movement before and after bracing, showing that the brace alters thoracic and lumbar kinematics during daily activities.[2]

angle.text: While worn, the brace holds the lower back and torso in a more upright position, which is how people use it for posture. The effect is present while the garment is on.

infobox: Elastic fabric, plastic or metal boning

paras: Medical corset braces descend from historical corsets, and metal corsets were sometimes used by doctors to correct posture.[1] Unlike traditional corsets, modern braces use elasticated panels for flexibility.[1]

A 2021 study of five adolescents (mean age 14.4) with spondylolysis back pain evaluated 3D thoracic and lumbar movement before and after corset bracing in daily activities.[2] A 2015 case report described a 24-year-old with multilevel spondylolysis.[3] Neither tests bracing for posture appearance.

Studies of reenactors and historical accounts reported that moderate lacing reduced lung capacity and that long-term use was linked to weaker core and back muscles and reliance on the garment for upright posture.[1] Reenactors reported significant discomfort when waist reduction exceeded about 7.6 cm.[1]

On T Nation forums, lifters discuss lower-back braces and belts for support, and one post describes wearing a lower back brace backwards during recovery from slipped rib syndrome.[4] Another thread notes that wearing a belt like a corset made breathing difficult.[5]
